title: Outward Spiral Matrix Walk
description:
You start at the cell `(rStart, cStart)` of an `rows x cols` grid facing east. The top-left corner is at `(0, 0)` and the bottom-right corner is at `(rows - 1, cols - 1)`.

You walk in a clockwise outward spiral to visit every position in this grid. Whenever you step outside the grid boundary, you continue walking outside and may re-enter the grid later. Specifically, starting at `(rStart, cStart)`, take 1 step east, 1 step south, 2 steps west, 2 steps north, 3 steps east, 3 steps south, and so on.

Return a 2D array of `[r, c]` coordinates representing every cell of the grid in the exact order it is visited.
hints: Notice the step lengths along the directions East, South, West, North follow the sequence 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, ...
Advance step by step along the current direction, recording coordinates whenever 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols until all rows * cols cells are collected.

examples.explanation: Starting at (0, 0) in a 1x4 grid, the walk visits (0, 0) then moves east through (0, 1), (0, 2), and (0, 3).
Starting at (1, 4) in a 5x6 grid, the spiral steps outside the right boundary and re-enters on the south and west legs until all 30 cells are recorded.
A 1x1 grid only contains (0, 0), which is visited immediately.
